questions.q: Why does this lesson add CloudWatch alarms in addition to the SNS NotifyFailure state already in the Step Functions state machine?
options: SNS notifications from Step Functions are unreliable and often fail to send
CloudWatch alarms are required by AWS for every Step Functions state machine
Alarms watch metrics independently of the pipeline's own logic, so they still catch failures even if the state machine never reaches its notify state
There is no real reason — it is purely redundant with no added coverage
questions.explain: The guide explains alarms are a second, independent layer: they fire even if the state machine gets stuck before its own Catch/Notify logic runs.

options: glue.driver.aggregate.numFailedTasks for the northfield-orders-etl job
Athena bytes scanned
S3 bucket size for northfield-raw-zone
ExecutionsFailed on the Step Functions state machine
questions.explain: The Glue failure alarm watches the job's own failed-tasks metric directly, scoped to northfield-orders-etl.

questions.q: What metric does northfield-stepfunctions-failure-alarm watch, and what does it catch?
options: ExecutionsFailed on the state machine — catching infrastructure-level failures that might occur before internal Catch logic runs
CPU utilization of the underlying EC2 instances
The number of successful Glue crawler runs
S3 PUT request count on the curated zone
questions.explain: ExecutionsFailed counts executions ending Failed, TimedOut, or Aborted — including failures that happen before any internal Catch logic executes.

questions.q: What does northfield-pipeline-dashboard combine into a single view?
options: A list of every IAM role in the account
Redshift table row counts only
Glue job duration/success-failure, Step Functions execution status, and Redshift/Athena usage metrics
Only S3 storage costs across all buckets
questions.explain: The dashboard combines Glue, Step Functions, Redshift, and Athena metrics into one screen covering the whole pipeline's health.

questions.q: Why does the lesson use two separate alarms (Glue and Step Functions) instead of just one?
options: They watch different failure surfaces — a Glue failure and a state-machine-level failure can each occur without the other showing up, so two alarms give broader coverage
Two alarms are cheaper than one in CloudWatch's pricing model
AWS limits each state machine to exactly one alarm type
One alarm can only monitor a single AWS account
questions.explain: The lesson explains a Glue failure can occur without the execution status showing Failed yet, and a state machine failure can stem from causes unrelated to Glue — so two independent alarms cover more failure modes.
